  Code: line 1369 (PIN_SHA jq expression)
  Problem: The jq expression iterates over matching runs twice — once for the non-cancelled branch and again for the fallback — which adds needless computation.
  Why it fails at runtime: While the script guards are working, the unnecessary double-pass means more GitHub API requests and CPU time are spent filtering than necessary. At current run sizes it's negligible, but scales poorly if the run list grows, violating YAGNI for intentional efficiency when a single filter pass could handle both branches via a more compact expression. The expression can be simplified to use conditional logic within a single map operation.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  Code: Lines 1349-1378 (PIN_SHA run-selection block)
  Problem: The fix only hardens the `PIN_SHA` path (lines 1349-1378), but the `else` branch at line 1372 still uses plain recency selection:
```bash
REVIEW_RUN=$(gh_api_safe "repos/${TEST_REPO}/actions/runs?branch=${PR_BRANCH}&event=pull_request&per_page=5" \
  --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name | test("Review|review|autofix|self-healing"; "i"))] | sort_by(.created_at) | last' || echo "")
```
  Why it fails at runtime: This leaves the poller behavior inconsistent. The exact hang scenario described (two review-type runs sharing the same SHA, one newer cancelled sibling masking an older success) can also occur on the no-PIN_SHA branch whenever multiple runs share the same head commit due to transactional workflow_dispatch queuing or concurrency artifacts. The same bug reproduction vector exists, creating future surprise when a future identical failure mode presents on the legacy branch.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  Code: Lines 1349-1378 (entire PIN_SHA conditional block)
  Problem: The new logic does not validate or handle the case where the API/JQ result produces empty or malformed JSON/object assignments to REVIEW_RUN.
  Why it fails at runtime: If gh_api_safe returns empty (e.g., API rate limit hit, pagination edge case, jq parse error where no branch matches), the REVIEW_RUN variable remains unset or empty. The subsequent polling loop code that relies on REVIEW_RUN being a valid run object would then dereference an undefined variable or attempt to validate an empty string, triggering shell errors or silent failures. Unlike the original code which had similar fragility, the absence of defensive `|| true` or validation in the jq expression means a transient empty response could cause the bash script to fail unexpectedly, corrupting poller state or triggering fallback to timeout behavior prematurely.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

- File: .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  Line or code reference: lines 1355-1378 (the new PIN_SHA jq filter and preceding comment)
  Problem: The jq filter uses `as $m` then duplicates the full array scan + name test + head_sha filter for non-cancelled and fallback branches. It also relies on `gh_api_safe` (which falls back to empty string on any transient error) combined with the outer `|| echo ""`, so malformed JSON or network hiccup produces empty REVIEW_RUN. The follow-on polling logic treats empty REVIEW_RUN as non-terminal ("Review run was cancelled — checking for newer run...") and continues the 30-minute REVIEW_TIMEOUT loop.
  Why it fails at runtime: On the exact repro case (two runs at same PIN_SHA, one success + one cancelled), the new filter works; however any API blip produces a stuck poller identical to the original bug. The comment correctly describes the concurrency cancel case but does not cover this failure mode.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  Line or code reference: lines 1369-1378 (gh_api_safe + || echo "" + subsequent if [ -n "$REVIEW_RUN" ] block)
  Problem: No explicit handling for empty REVIEW_RUN after a jq or API failure; the rate-limit backoff guard only triggers on RATE_LIMIT_BACKOFF > 0. Transient API errors (common at the end of a release when many workflows finish) cause the loop to spin with the same cancelled-run diagnostic until timeout.
  Why it fails at runtime: The release smoke-test Phase 4 hangs for the full REVIEW_TIMEOUT instead of backing off or surfacing a clear API-error state, exactly as observed on run 26989483268.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
